paper_metadata.title: Quantum Kernel Methods for Anomaly Detection in High-Velocity Data Streams

experiments.description: Hybrid quantum-classical quantum kernel anomaly detection evaluated on synthetic streaming datasets with varying feature dimensionality, nonlinear manifolds, and temporal patterns, compared against classical baselines.

algorithm.variant: Quantum kernel methods for streaming anomaly detection
algorithm.ansatz: parameterized quantum circuits with rotation-based encoding, entangling blocks, and data re-uploading

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical streaming features are normalized and mapped to rotation angles; temporal and distributional properties are incorporated via specialized quantum feature maps and window-based representations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Anomaly detection via quantum-kernel similarity estimation and one-class boundary/density-based classification in quantum feature space.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Not specified; concept drift handled through adaptive feature selection, parameter updates, ensemble weighting, and forgetting mechanisms.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic streaming anomaly detection on multivariate Gaussian mixtures, nonlinear manifold data, and temporal pattern sequences with controlled anomaly frequency, noise, and feature correlations.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic datasets generated with shifted-parameter anomalies, altered covariance anomalies, off-manifold anomalies, and regime-shift/pattern-violation anomalies; evaluated across varying feature dimensions (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 40).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalization to [0, π] for rotation-based encoding; dimension reduction and feature selection are described generally, but no exact pipeline parameters are reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Time-series cross-validation with multiple evaluation windows; performance reported using precision, recall, F1, AUROC, AUPRC, time-to-detection, prequential evaluation, and repeated experimental runs with confidence intervals.

noise_model.noise_type: simulated noise calibrated to current hardware characteristics

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data quality handling, missing-value imputation, noise reduction, normalization, scale standardization, dimension reduction (PCA/KPCA/Sparse PCA or autoencoder mentioned generally), feature selection, and feature engineering for temporal streams.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Kernel matrix construction, one-class SVM / density-based / graph-based / spectral / ensemble anomaly scoring, alert prioritization, and explanatory feature attribution.

speedup_claims.factor: quantum kernels may offer exponential representational advantage in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces
speedup_claims.conditions: for certain structured problems and sufficiently high-dimensional data
speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit asymptotic speedup is proven for the reported anomaly detection experiments; the paper discusses potential quantum advantage conceptually.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Implicit kernel evaluation in exponentially large Hilbert space; no explicit Big-O given
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical kernel methods scale quadratically or cubically with sample size; explicit best-known complexity not otherwise specified
